content:
## Read this before the manifests

Three things in the brief are contradictory or unnecessary. I've resolved them as follows — override me if your repo says otherwise.

**1. `s3.aws.upbound.io` is not ACK.** That API group belongs to the Upbound Crossplane AWS provider. ACK uses `s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1`. They are different controllers with different CRDs and a different resource model (ACK: one `Bucket` object carries versioning/encryption/PAB; Upbound: four separate objects). Since the task is titled "ACK-managed," I've written ACK. There's a Crossplane translation in the appendix if your repo actually runs `provider-aws-s3`.

**2. There is nothing here to SOPS-encrypt.** Bucket names, role names, account IDs, and OIDC issuer URLs are not secrets — they're identifiers that appear in every CloudTrail event. Encrypting them buys nothing and makes the overlays unreviewable in PRs. More to the point: IRSA exists *specifically* so there is no static credential to encrypt. If you add a SOPS-encrypted access key alongside an IRSA role, you've defeated the reason for the role. I've included the `decryption` stanza as a no-op comment so this Kustomization stays shape-compatible with your existing ones.

**3. I don't have your repo.** Paths, namespaces, the `GitRepository` name, and the ACK controller Kustomization name are assumptions marked `# ADJUST`. Everything else is drop-in.

---

## File tree

```
infra/s3/logs/
  kustomization.yaml
  bucket.yaml
infra/iam/logs/
  kustomization.yaml
  role.yaml
overlays/dev/logs/
  kustomization.yaml
  bucket-patch.yaml
  role-patch.yaml
overlays/prod/logs/
  kustomization.yaml
  bucket-patch.yaml
  role-patch.yaml
flux/kustomizations.yaml   # append two Kustomizations
```

The role lives under `infra/iam/` to respect your existing layout; the overlay pulls both bases so Flux still gets a single `path`.

---

## Base

**`infra/s3/logs/bucket.yaml`**

```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: myapp
    app.kubernetes.io/component: logs
spec:
  # spec.name is patched per-overlay. kustomize namePrefix/nameSuffix only
  # rewrites metadata.name, not the ACK spec field that names the AWS resource.
  name: REPLACED-BY-OVERLAY

  versioning:
    status: Enabled

  encryption:
    rules:
      - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
          sseAlgorithm: AES256

  publicAccessBlock:
    blockPublicACLs: true
    blockPublicPolicy: true
    ignorePublicACLs: true
    restrictPublicBuckets: true

  ownershipControls:
    rules:
      - objectOwnership: BucketOwnerEnforced

  # Versioning on a log bucket accumulates noncurrent versions forever.
  # These two rules are the difference between a $4/mo bucket and a $400/mo one.
  lifecycle:
    rules:
      - id: expire-noncurrent-versions
        status: Enabled
        filter:
          prefix: ""
        noncurrentVersionExpiration:
          noncurrentDays: 30
      - id: abort-incomplete-multipart
        status: Enabled
        filter:
          prefix: ""
        abortIncompleteMultipartUpload:
          daysAfterInitiation: 7

  tagging:
    tagSet:
      - key: app
        value: myapp
      - key: component
        value: logs
      - key: managed-by
        value: ack
```

**`infra/s3/logs/kustomization.yaml`**

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - bucket.yaml
```

**`infra/iam/logs/role.yaml`**

```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: myapp
    app.kubernetes.io/component: logs
spec:
  name: REPLACED-BY-OVERLAY
  description: IRSA role granting myapp read/write on its logs bucket
  maxSessionDuration: 3600
  # A path lets you scope the ACK iam-controller's own permissions to
  # iam:CreateRole on arn:aws:iam::*:role/myapp/* instead of *.
  path: /myapp/

  # Both documents are replaced wholesale by the overlays. They are
  # deliberately empty here so a mis-wired overlay fails closed.
  assumeRolePolicyDocument: |
    {"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[]}
  inlinePolicies:
    logs-bucket-rw: |
      {"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[]}

  tags:
    - key: app
      value: myapp
    - key: component
      value: logs
    - key: managed-by
      value: ack
```

**`infra/iam/logs/kustomization.yaml`**

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
resources:
  - role.yaml
```

---

## Dev overlay

**`overlays/dev/logs/kustomization.yaml`**

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: myapp-dev            # ADJUST
resources:
  - ../../../infra/s3/logs
  - ../../../infra/iam/logs
labels:
  - pairs:
      app.kubernetes.io/instance: myapp-dev
    includeSelectors: false
patches:
  - path: bucket-patch.yaml
  - path: role-patch.yaml
```

**`overlays/dev/logs/bucket-patch.yaml`**

```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
  annotations:
    # ACK resolves region per-resource from this annotation, falling back to
    # the controller's own region. Set it explicitly so the bucket doesn't
    # silently follow the controller if you move it.
    services.k8s.aws/region: us-east-1
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
```

**`overlays/dev/logs/role-patch.yaml`**

```yaml
apiVersion: iam.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-dev
  assumeRolePolicyDocument: |
    {
      "Version": "2012-10-17",
      "Statement": [
        {
          "Effect": "Allow",
          "Principal": {
            "Federated": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:oidc-provider/oidc.eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/id/DEV_OIDC_ID"
          },
          "Action": "sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity",
          "Condition": {
            "StringEquals": {
              "oidc.eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/id/DEV_OIDC_ID:aud": "sts.amazonaws.com",
              "oidc.eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/id/DEV_OIDC_ID:sub": "system:serviceaccount:myapp-dev:myapp-logs"
            }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  inlinePolicies:
    logs-bucket-rw: |
      {
        "Version": "2012-10-17",
        "Statement": [
          {
            "Sid": "BucketLevel",
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": ["s3:ListBucket", "s3:GetBucketLocation"],
            "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev"
          },
          {
            "Sid": "ObjectRW",
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": [
              "s3:GetObject",
              "s3:PutObject",
              "s3:DeleteObject",
              "s3:AbortMultipartUpload"
            ],
            "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::myapp-logs-dev/*"
          }
        ]
      }
```

---

## Prod overlay

**`overlays/prod/logs/kustomization.yaml`**

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: myapp-prod           # ADJUST
resources:
  - ../../../infra/s3/logs
  - ../../../infra/iam/logs
labels:
  - pairs:
      app.kubernetes.io/instance: myapp-prod
    includeSelectors: false
patches:
  - path: bucket-patch.yaml
  - path: role-patch.yaml
```

**`overlays/prod/logs/bucket-patch.yaml`**

```yaml
apiVersion: s3.services.k8s.aws/v1alpha1
kind: Bucket
metadata:
  name: myapp-logs
  annotations:
    services.k8s.aws/region: us-east-1
    # Deleting the CR will NOT delete the AWS bucket. Non-negotiable for
    # a prod log store — a bad `flux delete` or a pruned path is otherwise
    # an unrecoverable data loss event.
    services.k8s.aws/deletion-policy: retain
spec:
  name: myapp-logs-prod
  # Public access block covers ACL/policy-based exposure; this closes
  # pl
